issues.description: No stated specification for the new $ref-propagation algorithm; correctness rests on inline snapshots
issues.detail: The author cannot — and the diff does not — state the precondition, postcondition, or invariant of `flattenRef`. The function is now recursive, mutates `seen.ref` to null mid-recursion as a sentinel, traverses a second `seen.parent` chain, and conditionally deletes keys by structural equality. There is no comment explaining what property holds at entry vs. exit, nor what `ref === null` means versus `ref === undefined` (the type was just narrowed from `$ZodType | undefined | null` to `$ZodType | null` for `ref` while `parent` is `$ZodType | undefined` — an inconsistency that itself signals unreasoned design). The claim of correctness is `toMatchInlineSnapshot`. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: `flattenRef` recursion has no proven termination function
issues.detail: `flattenRef` now calls itself on `seen.ref` AND on `seen.parent`, with the `seen.ref = null` sentinel intended to prevent re-entry. But `seen.parent` is never nulled, and the second branch calls `flattenRef(seen.parent)` unconditionally when `seen.parent !== ref`. If a parent's parent points back into an already-visited node via a different edge, or if `parent` and `ref` form interleaved chains, termination depends on the graph shape, not on a decreasing measure the code maintains. State the well-founded order on (schema, edge-kind) and prove the recursive call strictly decreases it, or refuse the change.

issues.description: Structural equality via `JSON.stringify` used as a correctness primitive
issues.detail: Two separate de-duplication blocks decide whether to `delete schema[key]` by comparing `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. `JSON.stringify` is order-sensitive for objects, lossy for `undefined`, throws on cycles, and silently mis-handles `NaN`, `Infinity`, `BigInt`, and any non-enumerable property. Using it as the equality relation for whether a JSON Schema field is 'the same as' the definition's field is not reasoning — it is a vibe. Define the equality you actually need and implement it; otherwise this will silently produce wrong schemas whenever key order differs between parent and child.

issues.description: `overrideCount` test expectation doubled from 6 to 12 without justification
issues.detail: The test `override: do not run on references` previously asserted `overrideCount === 6`; the diff changes it to 12 and the rest of `finalize` removes the `if (!seen.isParent)` guard around `ctx.override(...)`. That guard's whole purpose was 'do not run override on references / parent nodes.' The test name still says 'do not run on references' yet the count doubled — which strongly suggests override now DOES run on parent nodes. Either the test name is now a lie, or the user-facing override contract has silently changed. State which, and update the test name and the public contract accordingly. As written, this is a silent semantic change shipped under a refactor.

issues.description: Smuggled goto: `seen.ref = null` as a mid-function recursion sentinel
issues.detail: The pattern `const ref = seen.ref; seen.ref = null; if (ref) { flattenRef(ref); ... }` is a flag mutating shared state to break recursion — a goto in polite clothing. The same node is now reachable along both the `ref` edge and the `parent` edge, and the sentinel only blocks one of them. Replace with an explicit visited-set parameter and an invariant ('flattenRef is called at most once per (node, edge)'), or prove that mutating the seen-map mid-traversal preserves the invariants of every other consumer of `ctx.seen`. SMUGGLED-GOTO.

issues.description: `isParentRef` computed via `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref` after `process` already recorded `result.parent`
issues.detail: The information 'is this edge the parent edge' is already stored on `seen` as of this PR (`result.parent = parent`). Recomputing it by reaching back through `_zod.parent` with an `as any` cast duplicates the source of truth and invites the two to disagree under cloning. Read it from `seen.parent === ref` instead, and drop the `any` cast — or document precisely why the cast is required and why the two sources cannot diverge.

issues.description: Mini and classic constructors now disagree on a previously-commented-out flag with no explanation
issues.detail: `mini/schemas.ts` uncomments `{ parent: true }` and `classic/schemas.ts` adds `{ parent: true }`. The classic diff lacks any prose, the mini diff merely removes a `// { parent: true }` comment, and there is no test asserting that mini's behaviour matches classic on the new `roJobId` case. If `{ parent: true }` was previously disabled deliberately in mini, the reason has been deleted along with the comment. State the invariant 'classic and mini produce identical JSON Schema for a check-augmented type' and add a test that enforces it, or document the divergence.

issues.description: `fileProcessor` change relocates shared properties to the parent of `anyOf` with no spec for the resulting shape
issues.detail: The new shape places `contentEncoding`, `format`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `type` as siblings of `anyOf`, with each `anyOf` branch carrying only `contentMediaType`. Per JSON Schema semantics this means validation must pass the outer constraints AND one of the branches — which happens to coincide for the test case, but the postcondition 'a value is accepted iff it is a string of the right length/encoding with one of the listed mime types' was never written down. Snapshot equality is not a proof. Write the postcondition and a property test against it; only then is the simplification justified.

issues.description: `play.ts` switched from package import to relative source import and left as a debug script
issues.detail: `play.ts` now imports from `./packages/zod/src/index.js` and contains `console.log`-driven manual verification of the very behaviour the PR claims to fix. This is the author admitting the change was validated by eyeballing stdout. It should not land in the repo, and its presence here is evidence the correctness argument is informal.

issues.description: Type of `Seen.ref` narrowed from `$ZodType | undefined | null` to `$ZodType | null` while `parent` is `$ZodType | undefined`
issues.detail: Two adjacent fields now use opposite conventions for 'absent.' `ref` uses `null` as 'already processed' (a sentinel) and presumably also as 'never set' since `undefined` was removed. `parent` uses `undefined`. A reader cannot tell from the types which absence means what. Pick one convention and document it, or model the state with a discriminated union.

review.summary: REFUSED as currently presented. The PR makes a substantive behavioural change to `$ref`/parent propagation in JSON Schema generation, yet ships without a stated specification, without an invariant for the now-recursive `flattenRef`, without a termination argument across the joined `ref`/`parent` graph, and with `JSON.stringify` used as the equality relation for de-duplication. The override-count expectation silently doubles from 6 to 12 under a test still titled 'do not run on references,' which indicates the public override contract has changed; that change must be made explicit or reverted. The `fileProcessor` simplification, the mini/classic `{ parent: true }` realignment, and the `play.ts` debug script all corroborate that this is TESTED-NOT-PROVED. What would have to change: state precondition/postcondition/invariant for `flattenRef`; replace the `seen.ref = null` mid-recursion sentinel with an explicit visited set; replace `JSON.stringify` equality with a defined relation; reconcile the override-on-parent semantics with the test name and document it; add a mini-vs-classic equivalence test; remove `play.ts`.
